title: Test suites effectiveness evolution in open source systems: empirical study
authors: Akour, M.; Alenezi, M.

title: Is mutation an appropriate tool for testing experiments?

title: Rotten green tests in Java, Pharo and Python

supporting_sentence: The presence of a rotten green test is a test smell, and a bad one, because the existence of a test gives us false confidence that the code under test is valid, when in fact that code may not have been tested at all.
relevance: Cross-language proof that assertion-less passing tests exist in Java and Python; validates vacuous-oracle drift as a real phenomenon.

title: Test Code Quality and Its Relation to Issue Handling Performance
authors: Athanasiou, D.; Nugroho, A.; Visser, J.; Zaidman, A.

title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey

title: An empirical analysis of the distribution of unit test smells and their impact on software maintenance

title: Are test smells really harmful? An empirical study

title: Understanding Test Deletion in Java Applications

title: Characterising the Quality of Behaviour Driven Development Specifications
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Embury, S.M.; Konstantinou, N.
venue: Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing
supporting_sentence: Despite much discussion amongst practitioners and in the blogosphere, as yet no formal definition of what makes for a high quality BDD suite has been given.
relevance: Defines BDD suite quality principles from a practitioner survey; quality judged by criteria, never by fault-detection measurement.

title: Behaviour driven development: A systematic mapping study
authors: Binamungu, L.P.; Maro, S.

title: Paired Code Smells and Test Smells: A Fine-Grained Longitudinal Empirical Study

title: An Exploratory Study on the Usage of Gherkin Features in Open-Source Projects

authors: Pontillo, V.; Amoroso d’Aragona, D.; Pecorelli, F.; Di Nucci, D.; Ferrucci, F.; Palomba, F.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: The performance of the machine learning-based detector is significantly better than heuristic-based techniques, but none of the learners able to overcome an average F-Measure of 51%.
relevance: Demonstrates test-smell detection itself is unreliable (F-measure at most 51%), a direct threat to any smell-based drift indicator.

title: Test-driven development with mutation testing – an experimental study
authors: Roman, A.; Mnich, M.
venue: Software Quality Journal
supporting_sentence: The TDD+M tests achieved better coverage on the code from TDD groups than the TDD tests on their own code (53.3% vs. 33.5% statement coverage and 64.9% vs. 37.5% mutation coverage).
relevance: Precedent for mutation coverage as the outcome measure of test-suite quality in a controlled experiment (unit level).

title: Assessing architectural drift in commercial software development: a case study
authors: Rosik, J.; Le Gear, A.; Buckley, J.; Babar, M.A.; Connolly, D.
venue: Software: Practice and Experience
supporting_sentence: However, implementations often diverge from their intended architectures: a phenomenon called architectural drift.
relevance: Establishes drift as divergence between an intended and an implemented artefact; exactly the relation we posit between the scenario and step layers.

title: Smells in system user interactive tests
authors: Rwemalika, R.; Habchi, S.; Papadakis, M.; Le Traon, Y.; Brasseur, M.C.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: We also conduct an empirical analysis to assess the diffuseness and removal of these smells in 48 industrial repositories and 12 open-source projects.
relevance: Largest smell+removal study for system-level interactive tests (35 smells, 60 repos); BDD-adjacent but not Gherkin-scoped and no oracle strength.

title: Mutation testing in the wild: findings from GitHub
authors: Sánchez, A.B.; Delgado-Pérez, P.; Medina-Bulo, I.; Segura, S.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: we first performed a search for mutation testing tools, 127 in total
relevance: Documents which mutation tools practitioners actually use (PIT, Infection, Humbug), grounding our tool choice in observed practice.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Assertions as Oracles
authors: Shrestha, K.; Rutherford, M.J.
venue: 2011 Fourth IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation
supporting_sentence: In this paper, we report the results of one such experiment in which we exercise seven core Java classes and two sample programs with branch-adequate, input only(i.e., no oracle) test suites and collect the failures observed by different oracles.
relevance: Shows oracle-free suites detect almost nothing even when branch-adequate; direct precedent for measuring unassertive BDD steps.

title: A dataset of regressions in web applications detected by end-to-end tests
authors: Soto-Sánchez, Ó.; Maes-Bermejo, M.; Gallego, M.; Gortázar, F.
venue: Software Quality Journal
supporting_sentence: The comparative study shows that there are important differences between end-to-end and unit tests, such as their execution time and the amount of resources they consume, which are much higher in the end-to-end tests.
relevance: Documents the cost asymmetry of E2E suites; justifies our measuring oracle strength without executing whole E2E suites at scale.

title: On the Relation of Test Smells to Software Code Quality
authors: Spadini, D.; Palomba, F.; Zaidman, A.; Bruntink, M.; Bacchelli, A.
venue: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
supporting_sentence: we collect data on 221 releases of ten software systems and we analyze more than a million test cases to investigate the association of six test smells and their co-occurrence with software quality
relevance: Repeated-snapshot (221 releases) smell study relating smells to change and defect proneness; closest longitudinal design to ours.

title: Investigating Severity Thresholds for Test Smells
authors: Spadini, D.; Schvarcbacher, M.; Oprescu, A.M.; Bruntink, M.; Bacchelli, A.
venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Mining Software Repositories
supporting_sentence: To accomplish this, we first analyzed some 1,500 open-source projects to elicit severity thresholds for commonly found test smells.
relevance: Shows smell-detection rules need severity thresholds; cautions against unweighted smell counts as drift signals.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Manually Created Equivalent Mutants
authors: Straubinger, P.; Degenhart, A.; Fraser, G.
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
supporting_sentence: less than 10% of manually created mutants are equivalent
relevance: Human-produced mutants show a much lower equivalence rate than tool-produced ones; reinforces that equivalence prevalence is operator/tool dependent.

title: Revisiting the Identification of the Co-evolution of Production and Test Code
authors: Sun, W.; Yan, M.; Liu, Z.; Xia, X.; Lei, Y.; Lo, D.
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
supporting_sentence: Many software processes advocate that the test code should co-evolve with the production code.
relevance: Methodological warning: mined production-test co-evolution samples are noisy; we must not reuse naive co-evolution heuristics for BDD history.

title: An Empirical Study on Mutation, Statement and Branch Coverage Fault Revelation That Avoids the Unreliable Clean Program Assumption
authors: Chekam, T.T.; Papadakis, M.; Le Traon, Y.; Harman, M.
venue: 2017 IEEE/ACM 39th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
supporting_sentence: our primary finding is that strong mutation testing has the highest fault revelation of four widely-used criteria.
relevance: Mutation score beats statement/branch coverage at revealing real faults; grounds its use as the oracle-strength ground truth.

title: A comprehensive study of pseudo-tested methods
authors: Vera-Pérez, O.L.; Danglot, B.; Monperrus, M.; Baudry, B.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: pseudo-tested methods are significantly less tested than the other methods; yet, for most of them, the developers would not pay the testing price to fix this situation.
relevance: 28K+ method replication of extreme-mutation oracle weakness; establishes coverage can mask weak oracles, at unit level only.

title: Data-Driven Mutation Analysis for Cyber-Physical Systems
authors: Viganò, E.; Cornejo, O.; Pastore, F.; Briand, L.C.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: Our results show that the approach effectively detects test suite shortcomings, is not affected by equivalent and redundant mutants, and entails acceptable costs.
relevance: Mutation above unit level on black-box/interoperability interfaces; shows system-level mutation is an accepted idea in other domains.

title: Assessing architectural evolution: a case study
authors: Wermelinger, M.; Yu, Y.; Lozano, A.; Capiluppi, A.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: This paper proposes to use a historical perspective on generic laws, principles, and guidelines, like Lehman's software evolution laws and Martin's design principles, in order to achieve a multi-faceted process and structural assessment of a system's architectural evolution.
relevance: Operationalises Lehman's evolution laws as measurable historical drift metrics; the model for turning evolution laws into indicators.

title: Mutation Analysis for Assessing End-to-End Web Tests
authors: Yandrapally, R.; Mesbah, A.
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
supporting_sentence: We evaluate our dynamic mutation analysis framework on six open source web apps.
relevance: Mutation analysis of E2E/UI suites over six public web apps: higher-level mutation at scale already exists, but not scoped to BDD layers or history.

title: Predicting Co-Changes between Functionality Specifications and Source Code in Behavior Driven Development
authors: Yang, A.Z.; Alencar da Costa, D.; Zou, Y.
venue: 2019 IEEE/ACM 16th International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR)
supporting_sentence: Therefore, .feature files can be out-of-date, reducing the advantages of using BDD.
relevance: Closest drift work: predicts BDD feature-file/code co-changes (AUC 0.77) but never validates the predictor against fault-detection ground truth.

title: A study of equivalent and stubborn mutation operators using human analysis of equivalence
authors: Yao, X.; Harman, M.; Jia, Y.
venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: PARAPHRASE: Of 4,181 generated mutants, 1,230 unkilled mutants were manually checked; 946 (approx. 23%) were found equivalent and 284 (approx. 7%) stubborn.
relevance: Human ground-truth equivalent-mutant prevalence by operator; tells us which operators to avoid and what equivalence rate to expect.

title: Mining Software Repositories to Study Co-Evolution of Production & Test Code
authors: Zaidman, A.; Van Rompaey, B.; Demeyer, S.; van Deursen, A.
venue: 2008 1st International Conference on Software Testing, Verification, and Validation
supporting_sentence: In this paper we investigate whether production code and the accompanying tests co-evolve by exploring a project's versioning system, code coverage reports and size-metrics.
relevance: Founding co-evolution study using versioning plus coverage; supplies the churn-versus-coverage vocabulary our scenario-age indicator borrows.

title: Demystifying the adoption of behavior-driven development in open source projects
authors: Zampetti, F.; Di Sorbo, A.; Visaggio, C.A.; Canfora, G.; Di Penta, M.
venue: Information and Software Technology
supporting_sentence: In about 37% of the cases, we found a co-evolution between scenarios/fixtures and production code.
relevance: Closest prior work: large-scale BDD framework adoption in OSS plus scenario/production co-evolution; no mutation analysis, no oracle-strength measurement.

title: Assertions are strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness
authors: Zhang, Y.; Mesbah, A.
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 10th Joint Meeting on Foundations of Software Engineering
supporting_sentence: We find that the number of assertions in a test suite strongly correlates with its effectiveness, and this factor directly influences the relation
relevance: Core mechanism evidence: assertions drive mutant-detected effectiveness; our step-definition assertion metric is its transfer to BDD.

title: On Adequacy of Assertions in Automated Test Suites: An Empirical Investigation
authors: Zhi, J.; Garousi, V.
venue: 2013 IEEE Sixth International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops
supporting_sentence: The paper reports an empirical study on the Inadequate-Assertion (IA) problem in the context of automated test suites developed for open-source projects.
relevance: Names and measures the inadequate-assertion problem in OSS suites using mutation analysis; template for our vacuous-step construct.
